key_findings.detail:
Unlike c-Si modules where Na⁺ originates from the front glass cover, in CIGS modules the glass is the **substrate** (superstrate structure reversed). Na⁺ originates from the back-side soda-lime glass:

- Soda-lime glass (SLG) substrate: **catastrophic PID** at −1000 V, 85°C within 25 hours (efficiency collapses from 14.9% to ~0%)
- Borosilicate glass (BSG) substrate: **35× lower leakage current** (due to lower K⁺ mobility); only marginal degradation after 25 hours; slow PID after 600 h
- When normalized to **equal Coulombs transferred**, SLG and BSG produce similar degradation, confirming this is a charge-based (ionic dose) mechanism

- [[papers/IEEE-267-2998-2-s2.0-85051002389-2018-J-Potential-Induced Degradation of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells: Alkali Metal Drift and Diffusion Effects.pdf#page=2|Theelen et al. (2018), p.2]]

key_findings.claim: Mo Back Contact as Critical Gatekeeper
key_findings.detail:
The microstructure of the Mo back contact determines whether Na⁺ from the glass substrate can reach the CIGS absorber:

- **PID-susceptible Mo:** Higher Na and Ga content in seed layer; denser, more continuous crystallite structure; less grain boundary oxygen; closed grain structure impedes Na diffusion away from the surface
- **PID-stable Mo:** Higher oxygen content in grain boundaries; larger, less dense crystallites; greater inter-crystallite distance; open granular structure where oxygen "traps" Na, hindering migration into CIGS

- [[papers/MDPI-74-2828-2-s2.0-85078032594-2019-J-Influence of molybdenum back contact on the pid effect for Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cells.pdf#page=3|Mansfield et al. (2019), p.3]]

key_findings.claim: Migration Path through Mo: Charge-Threshold Behavior
key_findings.detail:
Na⁺ transport through Mo into CIGS is threshold-governed:

- **PID-susceptible Mo:** Degradation begins after **~2.7 mC/cm²** transferred; at 5.7 mC/cm² Voc and FF begin declining; at 8.9 mC/cm² Na segregates at ZnO:Al surface
- **PID-stable Mo:** Requires **>10× more charge** (> ~27 mC/cm²) before degradation begins
- [[papers/MDPI-74-2828-2-s2.0-85078032594-2019-J-Influence of molybdenum back contact on the pid effect for Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cells.pdf#page=4|Mansfield et al. (2019), p.4]]

Na⁺ ions accumulate primarily at the CIGS/CdS buffer layer junction:

- Na concentration at CIGS surface increases from **1.2 × 10¹⁹** to **4.2 × 10¹⁹ cm⁻³** under PID stress
- Accumulated cations expand the depletion region from ~500 nm to ~1.5 µm toward the Mo contact
- Cations compensate p-type acceptors, reducing hole carrier concentration
- At 21.1 mC/cm², Na segregates at the ZnO:Al (front TCO) surface with visible surface spots

- [[papers/MDPI-74-2828-2-s2.0-85078032594-2019-J-Influence of molybdenum back contact on the pid effect for Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cells.pdf#page=5|Mansfield et al. (2019), p.5]]

- **Negative bias (Mo as cathode):** Drives Na⁺ from glass toward CIGS junction — catastrophic degradation
- **Positive bias:** Minimal or beneficial effect; reversing polarity partially compensates accumulated charge and allows partial recovery
- Degradation is partially reversible by reversing voltage polarity

- [[papers/IEEE-267-2998-2-s2.0-85051002389-2018-J-Potential-Induced Degradation of Cu(In,Ga)Se2 Solar Cells: Alkali Metal Drift and Diffusion Effects.pdf#page=3|Theelen et al. (2018), p.3]]
